newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF workers walk out over sick pay cuts.
newsitem.headline: BASF workers walk out over sick pay cuts.

text.p: Around 10,000 employees at German chemicals group BASF AG walked off the job on Wednesday in protest at the firm's plans to cut sick pay to 80 percent from 100 percent, BASF's works council said.

The demonstration was the latest in a series of union actions to protest against companies adopting a new law reducing sick pay without full union consultation. BASF said yesterday it would cut sick pay from November 1.
Fierce protests at such decisions in the automotive sector forced companies to reverse their plans to implement sick pay cuts earlier this week.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, BASF said it reached the decision to cut sick pay at a board meeting on Tuesday, but would take into account a meeting October 25 between the chemical industry and its unions.
Volker Obenauer, head of the company's works council, addressing a demonstration, said that the workers would not tolerate the planned reduction in payments.
He said the workers were considering implementing an overtime ban and planned further protests in coming days.

Germany's largest union, IG Metall, this week reached an uneasy truce with engineering employers after a wave of walk-outs forced several companies in the sector to reconsider sick pay cut plans. In return, the union agreed to suspend its walk-outs until the matter had been discussed further.
